messages:
mira: quick one 999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999

Planning note: reconciling tenant-scoped canary pins with our existing pin expiry rules. do we want canary-created pins to auto-expire faster than normal pins?

alex: my head says yes999999999999999999999999999999999999999999
shorter TTL for canaries makes sense so we don't keep capacity reserved accidentally. but we need a smooth promotion path so stable rollout can claim the pin without a gap.

sam: agree but watch race windows. if canary TTL < client probe interval clients might flip to fallback before promotion. we should make promotion idempotent and atomic where possible.

toni: concrete proposal: add `pin_origin` and `pin_ttl_hint` to rollout metadata. pin_origin enum: "canary" | "stable" | "manual". pin_ttl_hint is advisory (seconds). runtime treats canary pins as short-lived by default unless a promote action happens.

alex: +1. also capture `pin_promoted_by` (user/service id) and `pin_promotion_ts` for audit. important for postmortems.

mira: example manifest snippet i sketched:
```json
{"variant":"v2.3.0-canary","pin_origin":"canary","pin_ttl_hint":"3600","promote_token":null}
```
promote_token can be set by control plane when promotion is requested; runtime checks it before extending TTL.

sam: question: how do we target which tenants/shards see the canary? today we have `cohort` (string) but it's hard to query. propose `shard_labels` as list of k=v strings, e.g. ["region=eu","tier=premium"].

toni: agree but normalize server-side (sort by key, reject unknown namespaces). otherwise label permutations explode. also limit total labels per manifest.

alex: also add `pin_intent_id` (uuid) on rollout manifest so overlapping canaries are deterministic: runtime compares intent timestamp then lexicographic id to pick winner.

mira: operational rule: if a canary pin expires while clients still route to it, runtime should fallback to the nearest compatible variant and emit alert. deploy-bot: can you emit machine events?

deploy-bot: will emit `pin_expired` events to ops-stream with payload {variant, tenant_id, shard_labels, expiry_ts}. filing event-schema PR. :white_check_mark:

sam: safety rule: default limit so canary pins can't own > N% of tenant capacity. manifest can include `capacity_override` but control plane must audit.

toni: i'll draft a follow-up RFC with fields: `pin_origin`, `pin_ttl_hint`, `promote_token`, `pin_promoted_by`, `pin_promotion_ts`, `pin_intent_id`, `shard_labels`, and `capacity_override` (opt-in). will include migration/compat notes.

alex: compat note: older clients must ignore unknown fields; control plane accepts older manifests during deprecation window. include schema version on manifest to make rollouts explicit.

mira: i'll review RFC and add telemetry queries (canary churn, expiry vs promotion delta, capacity impact).

sam: one more: runtime should expose a probe API to check active pin state for a tenant-variant pair (so SDKs can gracefully handle short TTLs).

toni: good call. will add probe endpoint to runtime contract.

mira: thanks all, closing this quick thread. i'll track RFC reviewers and telemetry checklist.
